title: Affine closed base-change data and the signed vertex insertion homotopy
statement: Let X be affine, i:Z→X closed, and W_a→X a finite family of closed immersions factoring through Z, with quasi-compact complementary opens for i and each W_a. Let A be any ring sheaf and D any Row i W A of [def-sfb-closed-intersection-augmented-row]. For each vertex a there exists VertexContraction D a, with all its specified BaseChange, restriction, unionIntersection, augmentation, back inverse, signed component, and every-degree homotopy fields. No covering hypothesis is imposed. This asserts only the affine vertex contraction, not row existence, exactness, open comparison, or affine-cover detection.

proof.text: Each intersection is closed and has quasi-compact complementary open, whose finiteness follows by taking a finite union of the original complementary opens. Over the affine base all closed members are affine, so both bases of the closed base-change square are qcqs. Apply the arbitrary-ring closed base-change mate to each intersection, including Z at the empty index. Transport its module objects to the actual inverse-image coefficient modules, retaining the specified unit sections. Its inverse-image square is delta, its section formula gives normalized, and the mate equation gives beta and mate. The fibre product with vertex a is the intersection indexed by insert a s. This follows from the product universal property for nonempty s; at the empty index it follows because the vertex factors through the monomorphism Z into X. These are unionIntersection. Transport the actual restrictions through these comparisons to obtain intersectionRestriction. Naturality of the counit and the composite-unit equation show that the transported faces are the same actual unit faces. They prove restriction_units and faces. For the empty summand the closed counit gives augmentation; its composite with the pulled-back unit is the identity by the triangle equation. Adjoining a vertex already in the intersection is the identity closed subscheme, so the restriction for adjoining a is invertible. Choose its inverse as back. Both inverse equations follow. Define h by its product projections. Its component at s is zero if a belongs to s, and otherwise is (-1)^(number of b in s with b<a) times the projection at insert a s followed by back s. Preservation of finite products by closed inverse image makes this a natural module map. This gives component_zero and component_insert, including the empty output and absent degrees. Check the homotopy identity on each projection indexed by J. If a belongs to J, only the term deleting a in dh survives and its two equal signs multiply to one; the inverse equation makes it the identity. If a is absent, deletion of a in hd gives the identity. For b in J, the other hd term and the corresponding dh term have equal maps by the commuting restriction square. If k is the position of b, their exponents are s_a(J)+k+[a<b] and k+s_a(J)-[b<a], which differ by one, so they cancel over every coefficient ring. At degree -1 this is the inverse equation for the augmentation; at the top degree every index contains a. Outside the finite range both objects are zero. Product projections jointly detect equality, so this proves contraction in every integer degree. Every construction uses natural linear maps, and hence gives all the stated naturality.

theorem closed_intersection_affine_vertex {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] {m : ℕ} (W : Fin m → Over X)
    (hclosed : ∀ a, IsClosedImmersion (W a).hom)
    (hfactor : ∀ a, Nonempty (W a ⟶ Over.mk i))
    (hqc : ∃ U : X.Opens, Set.range U.ι = (Set.range i)ᶜ ∧ QuasiCompact U.ι)
    (hqcW : ∀ a, ∃ U : X.Opens,
      Set.range U.ι = (Set.range (W a).hom)ᶜ ∧ QuasiCompact U.ι)
    (A : Rings X) (D : Row i W A)
    [IsAffine X] (a : Fin m) : Nonempty (VertexContraction D a)
